source.title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a real Hénon map, possibly of higher degree, that has a wild attractor: a Cantor set that attracts a set of positive Lebesgue measure but is strictly contained in a transitive set?
accepted.context_brief: wild attractors for real Hénon maps

evidence.quote: Question 1. — Can we find a Hénon map (of some degree) which admits a wild attractor, i.e., a Cantor set which attracts a set of Lebesgue positive measure and which is strictly included in a transitive set ?

accepted.question_text: Is there a short or conceptually quick proof that some parameters in the Hénon family admit an SRB measure?

evidence.quote: Question 2. — Is there a quick proof for the existence of SRB for some parameters of the Hénon maps?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist ε>0 and a locally dense set E of quadratic Hénon maps such that, for every map in E, all points in some set of Lebesgue measure at least ε have non-statistical behavior, meaning their empirical measures do not converge?

evidence.quote: Question 3. — Do there exist ε > 0 and a locally dense set E of quadratic Hénon maps for which every point starting in some set of Lebesgue measure at least ε has non-statistical behavior?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a real conservative polynomial Hénon map with an annular rotation domain, and is there an open set of such maps?
accepted.context_brief: annular rotation domains for conservative maps

evidence.quote: Question 4. — Is there a real, conservative, polynomial Hénon map with an annular rotation domain? Is there an open set of such real, conservative, polynomial Hénon maps?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an entire symplectomorphism of R^2 with a nontrivial annular rotation domain?

evidence.quote: Question 5. — Is there an entire symplectomorphism of R2 with a non trivial annular rotation domain?

accepted.question_text: Construct an entire symplectic automorphism of C^2 with no periodic point but with a nonempty set of Lyapunov-unstable points whose orbits stay bounded.
accepted.context_brief: symplectic automorphisms of C^2 without periodic points

evidence.quote: Problem 1. — Construct an entire symplectic automorphism of C2 without periodic point and with non-empty set of (Lyapunov) unstable points with bounded orbit.

accepted.question_text: For the real quadratic Hénon maps f_{c,b}(x,y)=(x^2+c-by,x), which maps are mildly dissipative? In particular, is every map with |b|<1 mildly dissipative?

evidence.quote: Question 6. — Which real Hénon maps fc,b are mildly dissipative? Is this property satisfied by all Hénon maps with |b| < 1?

accepted.question_text: If a mildly dissipative map f_{c,b} in the zero-entropy locus E0 is infinitely renormalizable, is it a limit of positive-entropy maps, and is it a limit of Morse–Smale maps?

evidence.quote: Question 7. — Let us consider any infinitely renormalizable mildly dissipative map fc,b ∈ E0. Is it the limit of maps with positive entropy? Is it the limit of Morse-Smale maps?

accepted.question_text: For any infinitely renormalizable mildly dissipative map in the zero-entropy locus E0, does the sequence of renormalizations converge?

evidence.quote: Question 8. — Let us consider any infinitely renormalizable mildly dissipative map in E0. Does the sequence of renormalizations converge?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a mildly dissipative map f_{c,b} in E0 that has arbitrarily deep renormalizations of odd periods?

evidence.quote: Question 9. — Does there exist a mildly dissipative map fc,b ∈ E0 which admits arbitrarily deep renormalizations with odd periods?

accepted.question_text: For any real Hénon map, does the closure of the set of periodic orbits support every invariant probability measure?

evidence.quote: Question 10. — For any real Hénon map, does the closure of the set of periodic orbits support all the invariant probability measures?

accepted.question_text: For a map f_{c,b}, if (p_n) is an infinite family of periodic saddles that are pairwise not homoclinically related, must their hyperbolicity degenerate in the sense that min(|λ_-(p_n)|,|λ_+(p_n)|) tends to 0?

evidence.quote: Question 11. — For any map fc,b and any infinite set of periodic saddles (pn) which are pairwise not homoclinically related, do we have min(|λ−(pn)|, |λ+(pn)|) −→n→∞ 0?

accepted.question_text: Describe the kneading set K of the Lozi map, that is, characterize all kneading sequences that occur.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. — Describe the set of kneading sequences K.

accepted.question_text: For the Lozi map, do any two distinct kneading sequences determine a unique parameter pair (a,b), and thereby determine all the other kneading sequences in K?

evidence.quote: Question 12. — Is it true that any two distinct kneading sequences determine a unique pair of parameters (a, b), and in that way govern all the other kneading sequences of K?

accepted.question_text: For the Hénon maps H_{a,b} in the Wang–Young parameter set WY, describe the kneading set K of all kneading sequences.
accepted.context_brief: kneading sequences for Hénon maps in WY

evidence.quote: Problem 3. — Describe the set of kneading sequences K of the Hénon map Ha,b, with (a, b) ∈ WY.

accepted.question_text: For Hénon maps H_{a,b} with (a,b) in WY, do any two distinct kneading sequences determine a unique parameter pair (a,b), and hence determine all other kneading sequences in K?

evidence.quote: Question 13. — Is it true that any two distinct kneading sequences of the Hénon map Ha,b, with (a, b) ∈ WY, determine a unique pair of parameters (a, b), and in that way govern all the other kneading sequences in K of Ha,b?

accepted.question_text: For the quadratic complex Hénon map H2(x,y)=(y,x+y^2), can one describe the dynamics near the origin in C^2?

evidence.quote: Question 14. — Can we describe the dynamics of H2 near the origin in C2 ?

accepted.question_text: Does the map H2(x,y)=(y,x+y^2) have small cycles, meaning that every neighborhood of the origin in C^2 contains a nontrivial periodic cycle of H2?

evidence.quote: Question 15. — Does H2 have small cycles?

accepted.question_text: Does H2 have both small saddle cycles and small elliptic cycles near the origin?
accepted.context_brief: saddle and elliptic cycles for H2

evidence.quote: Question 16. — Does H2 have both small saddle cycles and small elliptic cycles?

accepted.question_text: Does H2 have a Herman ring?

evidence.quote: Question 17. — Does H2 have a Herman ring?

accepted.question_text: If Θ is the set of irrational rotation numbers θ for which H2 has a Herman ring of rotation number θ, does Θ have positive Lebesgue measure, and more precisely is 0 a Lebesgue density point of Θ?

evidence.quote: Question 18. — Does Θ have positive Lebesgue measure? More precisely, is 0 a Lebesgue density point of Θ?

accepted.question_text: Assume H2 has a Herman ring with bounded-type rotation number θ. Can one find dissipative Hénon maps H(x,y)=(ay,x+y^2) with a close to 1 and a≠0 that also have a Herman ring with rotation number θ?
accepted.context_brief: persistence of Herman rings under dissipation

evidence.quote: Question 19. — Assume H2 has a Herman ring with bounded type rotation number θ. Is it possible to find parameters a ∈ D ∖ {0} arbitrarily close to 1 such that the dissipative Hénon map H : C2 → C2 defined by H(x, y) = (ay, x + y2) has a Herman ring with rotation number θ?

accepted.question_text: If a generalized Hénon map f is quasi-hyperbolic, is int(K+) a union of finitely many basins of sink orbits?

evidence.quote: Question 20. — If f is quasi-hyperbolic, then is int(K+) the union of a finite number of basins of sink orbits?

accepted.question_text: If f is quasi-hyperbolic, does the equality J=J* hold?

evidence.quote: Question 21. — If f is quasi-hyperbolic, is J = J∗ ?

accepted.question_text: If f is quasi-hyperbolic, can f have no wandering Fatou component?

evidence.quote: Question 22. — If f is quasi-hyperbolic, then is there no wandering Fatou component?

accepted.question_text: If f is quasi-hyperbolic, do its unstable slices satisfy a John-type condition?

evidence.quote: Question 23. — If f is quasi-hyperbolic, do the unstable slices satisfy a John-type condition (as in [19])?

accepted.question_text: If f is quasi-hyperbolic and dissipative and J is connected, do external rays land at J, and is J a finite quotient of the real solenoid?

evidence.quote: Question 24. — If f is quasi-hyperbolic and dissipative, and if J is connected, do the external rays land at J? Is J a finite quotient of the real solenoid?

accepted.question_text: For a holomorphic automorphism of a compact Kähler surface with positive entropy, is Condition 3′ equivalent to Conditions 1 and 2, and do the quasi-hyperbolic analogues of Questions 20, 21, and 22 hold for such surface automorphisms?

evidence.quote: Question 25. — Is Condition 3′ equivalent to 1 and 2? And do Questions 20, 21, 22 above hold for quasi-hyperbolic surface automorphisms?

accepted.question_text: If a real surface automorphism f has real entropy equal to the entropy of the complex map, must f be quasi-hyperbolic?

evidence.quote: Question 26. — If f is a real surface automorphism such that the entropy of fR is the same as the entropy of f, does it follow that f is quasi-hyperbolic?

accepted.question_text: For the connectedness locus M={(c,b)∈C^2 : J_{c,b} is connected} of the complex Hénon family f_{c,b}(x,y)=(x^2+c-by,x), is M disconnected?
accepted.context_brief: connectedness locus of the complex Hénon family

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1. — M is disconnected.

accepted.question_text: Is the complex hyperbolic horseshoe locus HC connected?

evidence.quote: Question 27. — Is the locus HC connected?

accepted.question_text: For each 0≤α≤log 2, is the real isentrope E_α={(c,b)∈R^2 : h_top(f_{c,b}|_{R^2})=α} connected?

evidence.quote: Question 28 (van Strien [138]). — Is the isentrope Eα connected for any 0 ≤ α ≤ log 2 ?

accepted.question_text: Construct an algorithm that gives a rigorous upper bound for the topological entropy of a real Hénon map f_{c,b}|_{R^2}.

evidence.quote: Question 29. — Construct an algorithm to compute a rigorous upper bound for the topological entropy of a real Hénon map fc,b|R2.

accepted.question_text: As (a,c) tends to (0,0), give an asymptotic expansion for the Hausdorff dimension of J^+_{a,c}; in particular, is there a uniform lower bound of the form dim(J^+_{a,c})≥3+h(a) with h(a)>0 near c=0?

evidence.quote: Question 30. — Give an asymptotic expansion of the Hausdorff dimension of J+a,c as (a, c) tends to (0, 0). In particular is there a uniform lower bound of dim(J+a,c) of the form dim(J+a,c) ≥ 3 + h(a) with h(a) > 0 in the neighborhood of c = 0?

accepted.question_text: Can one find a generalized complex Hénon map f, an open set U⊂C^2 intersecting J^+, and a holomorphic foliation of U such that J^+∩U is a union of leaves of that foliation?

evidence.quote: Question 31. — Is it possible to find a generalized complex Hénon map f, an open set U ⊂ C2 intersecting J+ and a holomorphic foliation of U such that J+ ∩ U is a union of leaves of this foliation?

accepted.question_text: Under what circumstances can there exist saddle points p and q, together with relatively open sets U⊂W^u(p) and V⊂W^u(q), such that U∩K^+ and V∩K^+ are biholomorphic?
accepted.context_brief: biholomorphic unstable slices within one map

evidence.quote: Question 32. — Under which circumstances is it possible that there exist saddle points p and q, and relative open subsets U ⊂ Wu(p) and V ⊂ Wu(q) such that U ∩ K+ is biholomorphic to V ∩ K+?

accepted.question_text: Given two generalized Hénon maps f1 and f2, under what circumstances can a local unstable slice of f1 be biholomorphically equivalent to an unstable slice of f2?
accepted.context_brief: biholomorphic unstable slices across different maps

evidence.quote: Question 33. — Let f1, f2 be two generalized Hénon maps. Under which circumstances is it possible that some local unstable slice of f1 ... is biholomorphically equivalent to an unstable slice of f2?

accepted.question_text: To what extent is a generalized Hénon map determined by its list of unstable multipliers, or by the list of moduli of its unstable multipliers?

evidence.quote: Question 34. — To which extent is a generalized Hénon map determined by the list of its unstable multipliers (resp. by the list of moduli of its unstable multipliers)?

accepted.question_text: For a sufficiently regular weight φ on C^2, prove existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium state μ_φ for a complex Hénon map, for instance for every Hölder continuous φ and perhaps under a bound on max φ−min φ.

evidence.quote: Problem 4. — Prove the existence and the uniqueness of the equilibrium state µϕ associated to any sufficiently regular weight ϕ (for instance, every Hölder continuous ϕ, and possibly with some bound on max ϕ − min ϕ).

accepted.question_text: Assuming the equilibrium state μ_φ exists and is unique for a sufficiently regular φ, do weighted saddle-point measures converge to μ_φ: e^{-nP(φ)} Σ_{x∈SP_n} e^{S_n(φ)} δ_x → μ_φ?
accepted.context_brief: weighted equidistribution of saddle periodic points

evidence.quote: Question 35. — Suppose ϕ is sufficiently regular, so that the equilibrium state µϕ exists and is unique. Is it true that (7) ... → µϕ ?

accepted.question_text: Is the equidistribution of saddle periodic points exponentially fast against Hölder observables, and is the analogous weighted convergence to μ_φ also exponentially fast?

evidence.quote: Question 36. — Is the convergence (6) exponentially fast against Hölder continuous observables? Is that also the case for (7)?

accepted.question_text: Show that μ_φ satisfies the central limit theorem for Hölder continuous observables.
accepted.context_brief: central limit theorem for equilibrium states

evidence.quote: Problem 5. — Show that µϕ satisfies the CLT for Hölder continuous observables.

accepted.question_text: Show that μ_φ satisfies the large deviation principle for Hölder continuous observables with zero μ_φ-average that are not coboundaries.

evidence.quote: Problem 6. — Show that µϕ satisfies the Large Deviation Principle (LDP) for Hölder continuous observables.

accepted.question_text: Do there exist norms on functions on the Julia set, bounded on Hölder functions and contracted by f_* (or more generally by f_*(e^{φ-P(φ)}·)) on the complement of an invariant line, with contraction stable under perturbation of φ?

evidence.quote: Question 37. — Do there exist norms for functions on the Julia set which are bounded on Hölder continuous functions, contract ... under the action of f∗ ... and such that the contraction is stable by perturbation of ϕ?

accepted.question_text: For μ_φ as in Problem 4, show that every Hölder continuous observable that is not a coboundary satisfies the local central limit theorem and the almost sure invariance principle.
accepted.context_brief: LCLT and ASIP for equilibrium states

evidence.quote: Problem 7. — Let µϕ as in Problem 4. Show that all Hölder continuous observables which are not coboundaries satisfy the LCLT and the ASIP with respect to µϕ.

accepted.question_text: For a polynomial automorphism f of C^d with d≥3, describe the growth type of the sequence deg(f^n).

evidence.quote: Problem 8. — Describe the growth type of the sequence {deg(fn)} for any polynomial automorphism f of Cd, d ≥ 3.

accepted.question_text: Is the dynamical degree of every polynomial automorphism of C^d a weak Perron number of algebraic degree at most d−1?
accepted.context_brief: dynamical degrees as weak Perron numbers

evidence.quote: Question 38. — Is the dynamical degree of any polynomial automorphism of Cd equal to a weak Perron number of degree ≤ d − 1?

accepted.question_text: If a polynomial automorphism f of C^d satisfies λ(f)=1, must deg(f^n) grow like n^k for some k∈N, and if k≥1 must f preserve a rational fibration?

evidence.quote: Question 39. — Suppose f is a polynomial automorphism of Cd satisfying λ(f) = 1. Is it true that deg(fn) ≍ nk for some k ∈ N? Moreover, if k ≥ 1, does f preserve a rational fibration?

accepted.question_text: If λ(f)=1 and deg(f^n) is unbounded for a polynomial automorphism of C^d, does there exist C>0 such that deg(f^n)≥Cn for all n?
accepted.context_brief: linear lower bounds for unbounded degree growth

evidence.quote: Question 40. — Suppose that λ(f) = 1, and deg(fn) is unbounded for some polynomial automorphism f of Cd. Does there exist C > 0 such that deg(fn) ≥ Cn?

accepted.question_text: Can one characterize the elements f in Tame(3) with λ(f)=1 in terms of their action on the CAT(0) complex C constructed for Tame(3)?
accepted.context_brief: Tame(3) and action on the CAT(0) complex

evidence.quote: Question 41. — Is it possible to characterize those f ∈ Tame(3) for which λ(f) = 1 in terms of their action on C?

accepted.question_text: For a generalized Hénon map f, describe all generalized Hénon maps g such that the associated compact complex surfaces S̄(f) and S̄(g) are biholomorphic.

evidence.quote: Question 42. — Let f be any generalized Hénon map. Describe the set of all generalized Hénon maps g such that S¯(f) is biholomorphic to S¯(g).

accepted.question_text: Does every non-Kähler compact complex surface admit a birational structure?

evidence.quote: Question 43. — Does any non-Kähler compact complex surface admit a birational structure?

accepted.question_text: For a regular polynomial automorphism f of C^d, construct a compact complex manifold S̄(f) containing the quotient S(f)=Ω(f)/⟨f⟩ as the complement of a divisor, prove uniqueness of S̄(f) up to bimeromorphism, and describe its complex geometry and deformation space.
accepted.context_brief: compactifying orbit spaces of regular polynomial automorphisms

evidence.quote: Problem 9. — Let f ∈ Aut[Cd] be any regular polynomial automorphism. 1. Prove that one can find a compact complex manifold S¯(f) ... 2. Prove that S¯(f) is unique up to bimeromorphism. 3. Describe complex objects on S¯(f) ... Compute its deformation space.

accepted.question_text: If f∈Aut[C^3] is a polynomial automorphism with λ(f)^2>λ(f^{-1}), prove the existence of a projective compactification X of C^3 such that the induced birational map on X has a super-attracting fixed point on the divisor at infinity.
accepted.context_brief: compactifications for polynomial automorphisms of C^3

evidence.quote: Question 44. — Let f ∈ Aut[C3] be any polynomial automorphism such that λ(f)2 > λ(f−1). Prove the existence of a projective compactification X of C3 such that the induced birational map f : X 99K X admits a super-attracting fixed point p on the divisor at infinity.

accepted.question_text: Over a number field K, can one construct infinite families of generalized Hénon maps of algebraic degree d having K-rational cycles of length at least d+3? More strongly, can one get maps with N_d periodic points where N_d−d→∞, or even N_d/d→∞, as d→∞?
accepted.context_brief: long rational cycles over number fields

evidence.quote: Question 45. — Over a number field K, is it possible to construct infinite families of generalized Hénon maps of algebraic degree d, and K-rational cycles of length at least d + 3? Can one construct maps with Nd periodic points, where Nd − d → ∞, or even Nd/d → ∞ as d → ∞?

accepted.question_text: Fix a number field K, an integer B≥1, and degree d≥2. As f ranges over generalized Hénon maps of degree d over K, is the number of periodic points P with [K(P):K]≤B uniformly bounded in terms of [K:Q], d, and B?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2. — Let K be a number field, let B ≥ 1, and let d ≥ 2. Then as f varies over generalized Hénon maps of degree d over K, the quantity #{P ∈ Per(f) : [K(P) : K] ≤ B} is bounded just in terms of [K : Q], d, and B.

accepted.question_text: Over Q, does the map (x,y)↦(y,y^2+c+x) have no rational point of exact period N except when N is one of 1,2,3,4,6,8?
accepted.context_brief: periods over Q for a specific quadratic Hénon map

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3 (see [91]). — Over Q, (x, y) 7→ (y, y2 + c + x) has no point of period N, other than N ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8}.

accepted.question_text: For all but finitely many δ∈Q, do all Q-rational periodic points of maps f(x,y)=(y,y^2+c−δx) with c∈Q have period dividing 2?
accepted.context_brief: rational periodic points for maps with parameter δ

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4. — For all but finitely many δ ∈ Q, the Q-rational periodic points of any f(x, y) = (y, y2 + c − δx) with c ∈ Q have period dividing 2.

accepted.question_text: Fix a number field K, B≥1, and d≥2. Do there exist ε>0 and C such that, uniformly over generalized Hénon maps f of degree d over K, the set of points P with [K(P):K]≤B and canonical height ĥ_f(P)<ε h(f)+C has uniformly bounded cardinality?
accepted.context_brief: uniform boundedness of small canonical height points

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5. — Let K be a number field, let B ≥ 1, and let d ≥ 2. Then, there exist an ϵ > 0 and constant C ... such that ... #{P ∈ (K)2 : [K(P) : K] ≤ B and ĥf(P) < ϵh(f) + C} is bounded uniformly, where h(f) is the height of the tuple of coefficients of f.

accepted.question_text: For the Hénon divisibility sequence a_n attached to a non-periodic point of a generalized Hénon map over a number field, under what conditions does log Norm(a_n)=o(d^n) as n→∞, and under what conditions does there exist an ideal b such that a_n divides b for infinitely many n?

evidence.quote: Question 46. — Under what circumstance is it true that log Norm(an) = o(dn) as n → ∞? Under what circumstance does there exist an ideal b ⊂ OK,S such that an|b for infinitely many n?
